A short guide to the screens and features of the app.
The ring shows today’s progress toward your daily goal. Below it you see distance, calories and your streak (days in a row with the goal reached), and a chart of the last 7 days.

Choose Week, Month or Year. In Month and Year modes use the arrows or tap the name to pick any month or year that has data. Tap a bar to see that day or month in detail. Below the chart you will find totals, the best day, the number of days with the goal reached and a history list.

While counting, the app shows a notification with steps, calories, distance and a progress line. Android needs it to keep counting in the background. To add the 3×1 widget with the same information, long-press the home screen, open Widgets and choose Step Counter.

Set your goal, height, sex and weight. Step length is calculated from height and sex (men: height × 0.415, women: height × 0.413). You can enter it manually after measuring your own step; the calculated value stays visible there. Distance = steps × step length. Calories are an estimate based on weight and distance.

Steps come from your phone’s built-in step sensor. Only steps that can be reliably attributed to today are counted. If the app was stopped (battery saver, force stop, restart from a development tool), steps made in that time may be skipped. To avoid this, allow the app to work in the background and do not force-stop it. If the number for today looks wrong, use “Reset today’s steps” in Data.
Backup and moving to a new phone

“Save statistics to a folder” creates a backup file in the folder you choose. Copy that file to the new phone, then use “Load statistics from a file” and pick it. Days that exist in both places keep the larger value, and your settings are restored too. “Export to CSV” saves a table that opens in Excel or Google Sheets.
In Appearance you can choose the theme (system, light or dark) and the language (system, English or Русский).
